cells: Part XIV – Services Under the Union and States

blocks.content: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions by adding Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution.

items: Article 243I mandates the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats.
Article 243K vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Panchayats in the State Election Commission.
Part IX of the Constitution does not apply to the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, as well as certain tribal areas.
Constitutional bodies derive their powers directly from the Constitution, whereas statutory bodies are created by an Act of Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 conferred constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions.
It added Part IX titled 'The Panchayats' and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution of India.
The Act mandates a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj at the village, intermediate, and district levels.
Provides for a minimum of 33% (one-third) reservation of total seats for women across all tiers.
Constitutes a State Election Commission (Article 243K) and a State Finance Commission (Article 243I) in every state.
